accepted_steps.derivation: A monotone path from (0,0) to (9,9) uses 18 unit moves. Reaching x=9 requires exactly 9 R moves because R is the only move that increases x; reaching y=9 requires exactly 9 D moves because D is the only move that increases y. Every sequence of 9 R moves and 9 D moves is monotone, ends at (9,9), and stays within nonnegative coordinates. Conversely, any monotone path determines its ordered move sequence. This correspondence is bijective: the move sequence reconstructs the successive coordinates, and each valid coordinate path gives one move sequence. Thus paths are represented exactly by length-18 strings over {R,D} with exactly nine R and exactly nine D. The convention D<R orders these strings lexicographically: compare at the first position where two strings differ, and the string with D at that position is smaller. The later constraints restrict this universe; step 1 only fixes the representation and comparison order.
accepted_steps.goal: Represent each monotone path as a length-18 string over {R,D} with exactly nine R and nine D; record lex order D<R.
accepted_steps.result: Paths correspond bijectively to strings s in {R,D}^18 with exactly 9 R and 9 D. Lexicographic order is first-difference order with D<R. The lexicographically first valid move string is the least string in the later-constrained subset under this order.

accepted_steps.derivation: Step 1 identifies a path with a length-18 string over {R,D} having exactly nine R and nine D, where character position k records move k. The constraint 'never take three R moves consecutively' says there is no index i such that moves i, i+1, and i+2 are all R. Those three positions in the move string are exactly the substring formed by positions i,i+1,i+2, so this condition holds iff the string contains no occurrence of RRR. Similarly, 'never take three D moves consecutively' holds iff no three consecutive positions i,i+1,i+2 are all D, i.e. iff the string contains no occurrence of DDD. Thus each forbidden triple of moves corresponds bijectively to an occurrence of RRR or DDD in the string, and conversely each such substring is a forbidden triple of moves. The two constraints are independent and together forbid both substrings anywhere in the move string.
accepted_steps.goal: Express the no-three-consecutive constraint as forbidding substrings RRR and DDD in the move string.
accepted_steps.result: The no-three-consecutive constraint is exactly: the move string contains neither RRR nor DDD as a substring.

accepted_steps.derivation: Re-derive from step 1: a path is a length-18 string s over {R,D} with nine R and nine D; position k records the k-th move. Let R(k) and D(k) be prefix counts in s_1..s_k. The path is at (R(k),D(k)) after k moves, since R increases x by 1 and D increases y by 1. Thus the path visits cell (a,b) exactly when some k satisfies R(k)=a and D(k)=b. Because R(k)+D(k)=k, this can only happen at k=a+b, so visiting (a,b) is equivalent to the prefix of length a+b having exactly a R moves. Since the prefix length is a+b, having a R moves also means having (a+b)-a=b D moves. Conversely, if the prefix of length a+b has a R moves and b D moves, then after those a+b moves the path is at (a,b). Therefore forbidding a visit to (a,b) is exactly forbidding strings whose prefix of length a+b contains a R moves, equivalently whose count-prefix (a,b) occurs. Applying this to the five forbidden cells gives: (2,2) forbids prefix length 4 with 2 R; (4,3) forbids prefix length 7 with 4 R; (5,6) forbids prefix length 11 with 5 R; (7,5) forbids prefix length 12 with 7 R; (8,8) forbids prefix length 16 with 8 R. A valid string must avoid all five prefix-count conditions. These exclusions are independent of the no-RRR/no-DDD condition and of the checkpoint condition.
accepted_steps.goal: Translate each forbidden cell (a,b) into a prefix condition: after k moves #R=a and #D=b; exclude strings whose prefixes reach those counts.
accepted_steps.result: For each forbidden cell (a,b), exclude strings where the prefix of length a+b has exactly a R moves (hence b D moves), i.e. the count-prefix (a,b) occurs. Concretely exclude: prefix length 4 with 2 R; length 7 with 4 R; length 11 with 5 R; length 12 with 7 R; length 16 with 8 R.
